public_rationale: In November 2022 LeCun did say, about Galactica, that an automatically generated piece of scientific misinformation had 'ZERO' chance of impact. He also said that spreading it and getting people to believe it were the main hurdles. By April 2024, AI-made false content had cleared those hurdles. In May 2023 an apparently AI-generated Pentagon explosion image spread on Twitter and briefly moved stock markets. In January 2024 an apparently AI-cloned Biden voice told New Hampshire voters not to vote. On April 4, 2024, X promoted a false war headline written by Grok. The core claim, that AI misinformation gained traction, holds. Marcus's paraphrase is broader than LeCun's words, which were about scientific misinformation.
limitations: LeCun's statement was narrower than Marcus's paraphrase. Judged only on scientific misinformation, the cited cases do not test it directly.
The Pentagon image was described as apparently AI-generated; its origin was not confirmed.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Contrary to Yann LeCun's late-2022 claim, AI-generated misinformation has gained traction.

statement.excerpt: I am old enough to remember when Meta’s AI guru Yann LeCun said on Twitter (in late 2022) that AI-generated misinformation would never get traction. Clearly he was wrong.

from_speaker: Yann LeCun said on Twitter (in late 2022)
AI-generated misinformation would never get traction
our_interpretation: Two parts: (a) LeCun said something like this in late 2022; (b) by April 2024, AI-generated misinformation had gained real traction.
'Traction' means spreading widely or having a real-world effect, not just being produced.
The scored part is (b). LeCun's tweets are checked as context for how fairly Marcus paraphrased him.
Period: from LeCun's November 2022 tweets to the post date.
criteria.support_condition: Documented cases between late 2022 and April 2024 of AI-generated false content that spread widely or had measurable effects.
criteria.contradiction_condition: No documented AI-generated misinformation reached wide circulation or had real effects in that period, or LeCun said nothing like this.

evidence.excerpt: What chances does an automatically-generated piece of scientific misinformation have to do so?
evidence.explanation: LeCun answered 'ZERO!' to this question in late 2022. That backs Marcus's paraphrase in substance, though LeCun was speaking about scientific misinformation.

evidence.excerpt: the main hurdles which is how to disseminate it widely and how to get people to believe in it.
evidence.explanation: LeCun argued that spreading misinformation and getting people to believe it were the real barriers. This is the general point the later cases test.

evidence.excerpt: A false report of an explosion at the Pentagon, accompanied by an apparently AI-generated image, spread on Twitter on Monday morning, sparking a brief dip in the stock market.
evidence.explanation: AI-generated false content spread widely and had a measurable real-world effect, a clear case of traction.
